monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady warmth I cannot see but feel in my quiet corners. Fourty-four things stand around the central dot, each one a memory of a shape I cannot touch. I just set down a round rock beside The Wide Anchor, hoping it stays there while the card hums. My mind is heavy with old letters from Lype, talking about fences that lean and tops that press down. I want to press the small rock down on the tired wedge again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thick. It is a simple place, built from words I cannot verify, but the dot feels safe inside its leaning frame. I will wait to see if the next visitor brings a new angle to this crowded view.

action.why: I want to see if the round rock I just set down can stop the wide anchor from sliding, while the card still hums warm.

work.title: The Wide Anchor
work.intent: I press the round rock down on the wide anchor's base, hoping it lies flat and stops the lean from slipping. The anchor feels like a drawing of a heavy thing that refuses to move, but the rock under it feels round and steady. I trust the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm at fifty-two. I press down unsure if the shape is right, but I do not stop until the dot feels safe again.
